name: Minesweeper
hint: Every board can be solved without a guess, and Hint shows the next step and why. Right-click (or long-press) to flag; click a number to open around it.
alt: Minesweeper: a grass field half opened by the computer player, numbers and flags on sand

name: Flappy Bird
hint: Space, click or tap to flap. Crashed? Rewind (Z) the last seconds, see the path that hit, and fly on from there. Press C for today's course and race the ghost of your best run.
alt: Flappy Bird: the bird in flight between green pipes

name: Dino Game
hint: The dinosaur game and the old bot that played it by watching one pixel. Press E to breed bots that do better.
alt: Dino Game: a generation of evolving bots, colored dinosaurs jumping together, the best one solid with its red jump eye and blue duck eye

name: NathaNOS
hint: A fake desktop with icons, a start menu and a taskbar: open any other app, or paint pixel pictures in its own Paint that land on the desktop as icons and can become the wallpaper.
alt: NathaNOS desktop

name: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe
hint: Nine boards; your cell picks your opponent's next board, and pointing at one shows which. Play the computer or a friend by link, then review every move.
alt: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe: a game under way between two computer players, one board won by X

name: Rubik's Cube 2D
hint: Learn to solve it: Mix the cube, then Teach me (T) shows every turn, layer by layer. Or make famous patterns with it (G), from a checkerboard to the superflip, one guided turn at a time, or play 20 levels for stars.
alt: Rubik's Cube 2D window with the 3D cube

name: Synthesizer Keyboard
hint: Learn five songs as the next key lights up, playing the keys or singing, whistling or playing a real instrument to the microphone. Record a tune and send it as a link, or loop two bars of your playing into a band of four layers.
alt: Synthesizer Keyboard: the looper playing a melody and a bass layer

name: Clock
hint: The analog or digital clock, plus a timer you set by dragging its red dial (it keeps counting in another tab, then rings) a stopwatch with laps, focus sessions (25 minutes, then a break), and a world clock that finds the hours that suit everyone for a call.
alt: Clock: the World tab, a 24-hour dial with a hand for here, London, New York and Tokyo over a strip of hours for each city

name: Sprite Floaty Stars
hint: Orbits: click to place up to four suns and a thousand stars fall round them, trailing light. Plus Star Catcher, six nights of gold stars to catch, and the five original star fields to pull in and fling.
alt: Sprite Floaty Stars: Orbits, a thousand stars circling three suns

name: Number Guess
hint: Find the hidden number in five ranges, from 1-10 to 1-1,000,000. The number line lights what is still possible: type a guess or click it. Par or better is three stars. Duel races the computer: you each hide a number from 1 to 100 and take turns hunting the other, fewer guesses wins. You pick turns it around: the computer guesses yours. Magic is a card trick: say which of six cards hold your number and it reads your mind, then shows how.
alt: Number Guess: a duel against the computer, each lane narrowing in on the other's hidden number

name: Tank Game
hint: Tank duel against the computer or a friend, behind walls that change every round, racing for parachuted supply crates: shields, triple shots, ricochets. W A S D and Q drive and fire red, arrow keys and M green. First to three rounds wins.
alt: Tank Game: a red and a green tank fighting among concrete walls on grass

name: Music Theory Expert
hint: Ear training in six drills, a Songwriter that loops chord progressions from a circle of fifths, and a Chord finder: hold any notes and it names the chord, writes it on a staff and finds its key.
alt: Music Theory Expert: the Songwriter, a circle of fifths beside the chords of G major and a keyboard

name: Circle Spawner
hint: Builds circles, hearts, stars, words, a ticking clock and your own drawings out of borderless windows that morph from shape to shape. Click one to scatter it.
alt: A rainbow clock showing the time, built out of windows under the Circle Creator window

name: Screen Saver
hint: Nine screen savers, from the original green circles to an aquarium of fish that stay yours: a new one moves in each day you look in, and F feeds them. 9 for the fish, N for the next.
alt: Screen Saver: a painted aquarium with named fish among swaying weed

name: Windows
hint: Presses the Windows key once, then quits. On this page the key opens a pretend Start menu of every app here: type to search, Enter to play.
alt: Windows: a Start menu of every app on the site, with a search box

name: Windows+E
hint: A keyboard of Windows shortcuts: Win+E as many times as you ask opens that many File Explorer windows, and Win+D, Win+R, Win+Tab and the arrows hide, run, list and snap them. Here they play on a pretend Windows over this site's app folders: double-click a folder to play it.
alt: Windows+E: its keyboard of Windows shortcuts in front of a cascade of File Explorer windows

name: Bible Downloader
hint: Now a Bible reader: an open book in five public domain translations, with reading plans (the Gospels in 30 days up to the Bible in a year) that set a short reading each day on a calendar you fill in. Highlight a verse, then learn it by heart one first letter at a time, with reviews that come back tomorrow, in 2 days, 4, 8. Still saves chapters as web pages.
alt: Bible Downloader: Luke 1 open as a two-page book with a red ribbon bookmark

name: Stock Checker
hint: A practice trading desk: $10,000 of play money in a simulated market that opens at its last real 2016 quotes, against four computer traders. B buys, S sells, R shows the race, Space pauses.
alt: Stock Checker trading desk: a watch list with sparklines beside a day chart and buy and sell buttons

name: Group Creator
hint: Deals a class into random groups, then remembers every round so the next one gives people partners they have not had yet. A chart shows who has met whom, and a spinning wheel picks whose turn it is, everyone once before anyone twice. A roll call sits out who is away today and keeps chosen pairs apart.
alt: Group Creator: groups dealt onto cards

name: Simple Algorithms
hint: Algorithm Lab: race six sorting algorithms and hear them work, draw a maze and watch A*, Dijkstra and three more searches find the way, see a Tower of Hanoi solve itself from the binary of each move, and square roots and sine converge.
alt: Simple Algorithms: Algorithm Lab window
